title: Village Sample Complexity for Detecting Heterogeneous Signed Spillovers over All Designs
banked_reason: The proved frontier is a matched all-design rate for exact linear-in-means responses on disjoint equal-sized cliques; it supplies no robustness guarantee for nonlinear responses or other network structures. Sound subfield result below fixed field floor; validity gate confirmed downgrade.
gap_reasons: The proved frontier is a matched all-design rate for exact linear-in-means responses on disjoint equal-sized cliques; it supplies no robustness guarantee for nonlinear responses or other network structures.
The menu equivalence and Bernoulli penalty remain coefficient-cube results, and qualifying-menu constants need not be uniform in village size, as the framing correctly acknowledges.

The projected score is constrained by the structural scope and missing practical power calibration: the conservative published-class sufficient threshold exceeds 8.8 billion villages at rho=1/8, while the enumerations check identities rather than establish operational sample-size guidance.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery discharged the all-design signed-energy rate, the exact count-menu elbow, the Bernoulli penalty, and transfer to the published outcome-bound linear class; the mathematics panel passed after both cited sources were verified. The field ambition failed on equal-clique linear scope, coefficient-cube menu results, nonuniform menu constants, adaptation of the published score, and conservative power thresholds. This is a sound subfield derivation, with no Lean formalization attempted; a higher-tier re-raise requires stronger theorem scope or practically sharper bounds rather than another framing retry.
tldr: On Gao et al.'s uniformly bounded unit-specific linear-in-means class, restricted to disjoint complete villages, the unrestricted-design village complexity satisfies \(N_{\mathrm{GHSW}}(k,\rho)\asymp\rho^{-4}\), uniformly for \(k\ge8\) and \(0<\rho\le1/8\). The target is squared causal spillover energy, which detects heterogeneous signed effects even when their average is zero. A computable three-count saturation design and conditional quadratic test attain size at most \(0.05\) and power at least \(0.95\); the converse permits every outcome-blind joint assignment law and every full-record randomized test. Achievability is proved directly on the full published class, and legal quarter-unit coefficient-cube mixtures transfer the converse to that larger class. A second result resolves the exact-count menu question for the coefficient-cube benchmark: under independent uniform labeled subsets conditional on the complete count vector, the fixed-menu frontier is finite exactly when \(\max\{|\mathcal R_0|,|\mathcal R_1|\}\ge3\), where \(\mathcal R_0=\mathcal R\cap\{0,\ldots,k-1\}\) and \(\mathcal R_1=\mathcal R\cap\{1,\ldots,k\}\). For each qualifying fixed village size and menu it has order \(\rho^{-4}\), with a computable menu-dependent upper constant. Menus of at most two counts and endpoint triples \(\{0,c,k\}\) have infinite frontier at every separation in the stated range, even for arbitrary full-record tests and correlated village counts. The supporting same-class Bernoulli comparison retains the coefficient cube and has village complexity of order \(k^2\rho^{-4}\).
gap: Gao et al. construct a Bernoulli energy test on a bounded-outcome linear-in-means class. Kandiros et al. optimize linear-contrast estimation. The missing object is matched finite-error RMS village complexity over every assignment law and test on complete villages, uniformly in village size.
fill: Conditional moment reproduction and legal compact-support mixtures supply an attaining design and an all-design converse. The published-class comparison establishes the same order under the larger outcome bound on disjoint cliques. The same-class Bernoulli comparison separates village replication from village enlargement. The menu question concerns a distinct randomized-saturation subclass and leaves the endpoint-information criterion open.
